primitives.name: Homographic Projection
primitives.verbatim_quote: The paper proposes formulating ice hockey MOT as a bipartite graph matching problem infused with homography: mapping player foot keypoints to an overhead rink template and encoding the projected positions into a graph network so that overlapping players in broadcast view become spatially separable in the top-down view.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in combining homographic projection with bipartite graph matching to disentangle occluded players in monocular broadcast feeds. Each frame is modeled as a bipartite graph where nodes represent players and edges represent candidate associations. The homography maps foot keypoints to a top-down rink view, resolving spatial overlaps. Message-passing networks refine these associations iteratively by updating node and edge representations based on neighbor information. This dual approach ensures robustness against occlusion while maintaining temporal coherence. Failure modes include inaccurate footpoint detection, incorrect homography estimation, or insufficient message-passing depth leading to poor association resolution.
